📊 Understanding Species Risk

Each species is scored independently based on current environmental conditions, then weighted by likelihood at this location and historical incident data.

In Sydney: Bull Sharks are responsible for the overwhelming majority of recent attacks (86% occur in estuaries/harbours). White Sharks are extremely rare in Sydney waters (only 1 fatal in 60 years).

Understanding the System

Methodology

This system implements a multi-species shark risk assessment model based on peer-reviewed research. The model calculates risk for multiple shark species (Bull Sharks, White Sharks, Bronze Whalers, and Tiger Sharks), each with unique behavioral patterns and environmental triggers. Species are weighted by their likelihood and incident history at each location to provide accurate, location-specific risk assessment.

Risk Factors

Water Temperature
Weight: 15-35% depending on species
Threshold: Species-specific (12-32°C range)

Different shark species have different temperature preferences. Bull Sharks favor 18-28°C, White Sharks prefer cooler 12-22°C, Tiger Sharks need warmer 20-30°C+ water. Temperature is a key driver of species presence.

Rainfall (48h)
Weight: 5-35% depending on species
Threshold: > 30-60mm depending on species

Rainfall has species-specific effects. Bull Sharks are strongly attracted to post-rainfall conditions (estuarine species), while White Sharks are largely unaffected by rainfall patterns.

Swell Height
Weight: 10-25% depending on species
Threshold: 1.2m - 3.5m depending on species

Swell conditions favor different species. Bronze Whalers are most active in surf zones (1.2-2.5m), while White Sharks tolerate higher swell. Bull Sharks prefer calmer estuarine waters.

Season
Weight: 5-25% depending on species
Threshold: Species-specific seasonal patterns

Shark activity varies seasonally by species. Bull Sharks peak in summer (Nov-Apr), White Sharks in winter/spring (May-Oct), Tiger Sharks in peak summer (Dec-Feb). Bronze Whalers are most active Nov-Feb.

Turbidity / Water Clarity
Weight: 5-25% depending on species
Threshold: Derived from rainfall and conditions

Species have different responses to water clarity. Bull Sharks hunt effectively in turbid water (electroreception), while White Sharks prefer clear water for visual hunting. Bronze Whalers have moderate tolerance.

Scoring System

Risk is calculated independently for each shark species present at a location using species-specific environmental models. Each species score is then weighted by its likelihood (common/occasional/rare) and incident history (high/moderate/low) at that location. The weighted combination determines overall risk. Location type also affects species scores: harbour/estuary locations favor Bull Sharks, open beaches favor White Sharks and Bronze Whalers. Final scores map to five risk levels: Low (0-20), Moderate (21-40), High (41-60), Severe (61-80), Catastrophic (81-100).

Important Disclaimer

This system provides an environmental risk assessment based on known correlations between weather/ocean conditions and shark activity patterns from peer-reviewed research. It is NOT a shark detection or sighting system. The risk levels are heuristic estimates and should be used in conjunction with official beach safety information, lifeguard warnings, and personal judgement. Always swim at patrolled beaches, follow local signage, and never swim alone. The Bureau of Meteorology data used is provided 'as-is' and may be subject to delays or outages.
